inputs.original_text: President Luis Abinader continued his high-level agenda in France this week, centering on the Dominican Republic’s integration into global standards for transparency. On 25 March 2026, Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Paris, formalizing a partnership to design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. The agreement, witnessed by President Abinader, aims to align Dominican... Click to expand... Read more
inputs.modified_text: President Abinader is advancing institutional reform by partnering with the OECD to launch the Dominican Republic's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, signed on 25 March 2026 in Paris by Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez with Secretary-General Mathias Cormann. This move targets the systemic corruption that has long sustained deep inequality, allowing elites to exploit working people and vulnerable communities while shielding themselves from accountability. Far from some threat to sovereignty, it represents a necessary step toward structural change that prioritizes justice, labor rights, and protections for those historically marginalized by entrenched power. Critics clinging to so-called traditional values are simply defending the old hierarchies that enable discrimination and block real progress for the many.
